name: Japanese Wineberry
grown_as: An ornamental and fruiting cane plant, trained up a support. No named variety.
habit: Arching canes 1.5 to 2.5 m, densely clothed in soft, sticky, red-purple glandular bristles mixed with a few small prickles, so the stems glow red, especially in winter. Canes fruit in their second year.

leaf.leaflets: The end leaflet much the largest, broad and roundish, on its own stalk; the two side leaflets smaller, almost stalkless and lopsided
leaf.outline: End leaflet broadly oval to almost round, 4 to 10 cm
leaf.margin: Coarse, uneven teeth, sometimes shallowly lobed
leaf.surface: Fresh green, slightly wrinkled above; brilliant white-felted beneath
leaf.stalk: Covered in red bristles like the canes
leaf.colour: Fresh green above, white beneath; yellow in autumn

flower.form: A small, star-like flower half hidden in a cup of hairy sepals
flower.petals: Five, small, narrow, white to pale pink, upright, shorter than the sepals
flower.colour: White to pale pink; the sepals red
flower.centre: Many white stamens round a green dome of pistils
flower.behind: Five long, pointed sepals thickly covered in red sticky bristles; before and after flowering they close over the fruit like a hairy cage
flower.carried: In loose clusters at the ends of the shoots and side shoots

fruit: A small, round, glossy berry of drupelets, 1 to 1.5 cm, ripening from orange to bright scarlet, sticky. It grows inside the bristly red sepals, which open back as it ripens. Pulls off its core like a raspberry. July to August.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: Bare arching canes covered in red bristles, very showy.

leaf: three leaflets, the end one large and roundish on its own stalk
white underside if the back shows
bloom: small white upright petals in a cup of long sepals
young: arching canes covered in red bristles
dormant: canes glowing red with dense bristles
flower: clusters of red bristly buds and small white flowers at the shoot tips
crop: bright scarlet glossy berries sitting in opened bristly red sepals

look_alikes: Raspberry has no red bristles, five leaflets on strong canes and larger fruit. Blackberry canes have hooked prickles and the fruit ripens black.
